reason.label: Observed (studies 027 and 028)
reason.text: Across v0.24.0 and v0.25.0 the original S1 search beat S2 and S3 at 8 and 12 states (at 12 states S1 X 3/12, U 0.158; S3 X 0/12, U 0.398). Building S4 on S3 builds on the losing lineage, so S4 is rebuilt on S1 and the headline compares S4 with S1.

scratch_diagnosis.label: Observed (scratch, smoke seeds 9590001-9590003, scale8 and scale12, 3 seeds each, 55 s eps 0; partly CPU-contended; never a gate input)
scratch_diagnosis.prior_partial_check: bd587ab (S2_ABLATION_028) ablated S2 internals only and never compared S2 or S3 with S1; this is the first S1-vs-S2/S3 mechanism check
scratch_diagnosis.mechanism: symmetry-breaking clauses. S2/S3's BFS-canonical clauses (auxiliaries t, p, mm; O(n^3 k) clauses) make the SAT witness solves that answer support queries slow. Removing only those clauses (S2_nobfs) moved S2 from U counts [134, 227, 229] to [0, 97, 164] at 12 states (S1: [20, 54, 174]) and from [2, 4, 74] to [0, 0, 0] at 8 states. The same mechanism, weaker, is inside S1: removing S1's first-visit symmetry (S1_nosym) moved S1 at 12 states from [20, 54, 174] to [0, 0, 61].

not_the_mechanism.lower_bound_proofs: UNSAT solves are few and cheap (mean 0-3.3 s per run at 12 states; S1 had 0 UNSAT solves: at a 16-state bound every code stays possible in these worlds)
not_the_mechanism.support_chain: the _chain suffix witness is cheap (028 scratch) and S2_nodist / S2_g3 changed little or hurt
not_the_mechanism.incremental_solver: a fresh solver per step (S2_fresh) helped at 8 states ([2, 4, 74] -> [0, 0, 0]) but not at 12 states ([134, 227, 229] -> [136, 160, 249]): a secondary cost at 8 states only

scratch_diagnosis.time_split: S2 at 12 states: per run mean 35.2 s in SAT support solves, 23.3 s in solves cut by the deadline (UNKNOWN), 3.3 s in UNSAT; S1: 48.9 s in 1932 SAT solves, 7.3 s building one CNF per step
scratch_diagnosis.consequence: S4 keeps the S1 encoding as instructed (first-visit symmetry included). A pre-declared secondary arm S4_nosym (S4 with RegionK symmetry=False; same projection, so the same exact answers) measures the diagnosed mechanism; it is descriptive here and is the candidate for v0.27.0.

arms.S4: brute/scalesearch4.py ScaleRegion4(16): the frozen S1 RegionK encoding (brute.region, imported unchanged) plus (i) one lazily built solver per step answering every query by assumptions; (ii) witness reuse: every SAT model is a concrete <=16-state machine kept in a pool of 32, re-simulated on each reading and used as a witness for every action (unexercised transitions witness visited-state codes, and all codes when a state is unvisited); (iii) several queries in one solve: one assumption OR(nc[b][c] : c not yet witnessed), UNSAT proves them all impossible, SAT witnesses one code and is harvested, repeat; (iv) S3's hard 10 s per-query wall cap by conflict chunks with a wall check before each chunk, plus S1's 100000-conflict budget per solve. Solver: chosen on smoke seeds before the source freeze, among g3 (S1's) and m22; recorded in deviation #130
arms.S4_nowit: ablation: S4 without witness reuse (no pool, no harvesting beyond the single code a SAT answer shows)
arms.S4_nosym: secondary, descriptive: S4 with symmetry=False (tests the scratch diagnosis)
arms.S2: dropped from the run for runtime (S3 is the frozen exact control; S2 equals S3 on exact answers in study 028)
